svg.title: How HoMe Improves Optimization and Evaluation Efficiency
svg.desc: Candidates pass smoke tests and early mechanism admission checks. Adaptive sampling selects cases and queries using historical performance. Construction-equivalent memory is reused with a probability; otherwise memory is rebuilt. Parallel queries and scoring produce evidence for further diagnosis and final selection. Aggregate sampled scores cannot directly rank candidates.
svg.text: Efficient Evaluation: Screen, Sample, and Reuse
Screen committed candidates
Smoke test: a few real sessions and questions
Early stage: mechanism changes and needed repairs
Rejected → Return reasons and revise
Adaptively sample cases and queries
Prioritize failures, stale units, and sparse observations
Select cases first, then queries within the cap
Retain exploration and check for regressions
Check construction equivalence against evaluated ancestors
Inspect construction paths in code, prompts, and configuration; rebuild when equivalence is uncertain
Equivalent: reuse with a probability
Restore the ancestor's constructed memory
Retain reuse provenance and version links
Changed, or no reuse this round
Process original sessions and rebuild memory
Save a new session-level memory history
Run retrieval, answering, and scoring in parallel; record evidence
Scores, query tokens, and traces → Update history → Next diagnosis / Final selection
Compare shared cases and queries, coverage, difficulty, and regressions. Do not rank by aggregate sampled scores.
The Experiment Manager plans admission, sampling, and reuse; the Evaluation Environment executes each run.
